podcast.body: Released on David Bowie's 69th birthday, January 8th, 2016, this album was secretly recorded with producer Tony Visconti after Bowie's liver cancer diagnosis in mid-2014, becoming his "last will and testament" once he learned his cancer was terminal. The album is suffused with lyrics about death and some of the most "ghostly vocals" Bowie ever recorded. A week after his death, it debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, knocking Adele's "25" from the top spot, and was critically acclaimed as one of his best LPs and a seminal meditation on death. "That title, Blackstar, would also double as the title of the next David Bowie album, which was announced in October 2015, accompanied by a music video for Blackstar."

podcast.body: The album's cover features a large Blackstar on a white background, with a star cut into five pieces below it that spell out "Bowie" upon close inspection. Exposing the vinyl to light produces a star-like reflection, or possibly a bird, while exposing the cover to sunlight causes the star to fade, revealing a starry sky; under black light, it shines like a star at night. The CD reportedly smells like black licorice when first opened. One font used on the back sleeve is called "Terminal" and belongs to a design suite named "Lazarus." The gatefold liner reveals Bowie's image on the right reflected eerily onto a star field on the left, where connecting the biggest stars forms a stick figure, reminiscent of Starman. "There are other things lurking, just waiting to be found."

podcast.body: This album is musically, lyrically, and structurally complex, seen by Bowie as a final, independent legacy, distinct from his previous work. It incorporates influences from electronic jazz, rap, hip hop, drum and bass, and other electronic music. The recording process was complicated, involving many musicians including a New York jazz group, and only Tony Visconti was aware of Bowie's terminal illness during this period. The album achieved massive commercial success, becoming the best-selling vinyl album of 2016, more than doubling the sales of Adel's top-selling album from the previous year. "No tiene nada que ver con lo que había hecho de David Bowie anteriormente, musicalmente, liricamente, estructuralmente es algo complicadísimo y yo creo que él quería dejarnos algo completamente independiente de lo que había hecho como último legado."

This album was released on Friday, January 14, 2016, just two days before Bowie's death. It is an excellent record that contains numerous lyrical and thematic references to mortality and his impending death. "His last album, Blackstar, came out on Friday, January 14th, 2016, two days before he died."

podcast.title: Final Album
podcast.body: This album was written and recorded by Bowie after he received a diagnosis of liver cancer in summer 2014, knowing he likely had time for only one more album. He worked at The Magic Shop on Crosby Street, with a daily routine, finishing the album before news from his doctors in November 2015 confirmed his cancer was terminal. The album was released on January 8th, 2016, his 69th birthday, and contained tracks with ominous videos and lyrics reflecting his mortality, such as "Lazarus." "And then, that a new album called Blackstar would be released on January 8th, 2016, Bowie 69th birthday."
